reason: The PROBLEM is proven, but the FIX's numbers are wrong against the real source, so the finding is refuted with the corrected fix below. On the problem I went past the seat's measureText heuristic and parsed the cmap out of the three vendored woff2 files directly (brotli-decompress, walk the table directory, read format-4/12 subtables): Geist-Regular, Geist-SemiBold and GeistMono-Regular each map 726/726/887 codepoints and NONE of them carries U+2302, U+270E or U+2611; all three carry U+2197. So three of the four marks in shell()'s `<nav class="rail">` (lately.html:710) are painted by an OS fallback, not by a face the studio chose. The inherited stack is `"Geist", system-ui, sans-serif` (lately.html:117), and .rail i (lately.html:157) only sets font-size 13px, so nothing intercepts the fallback. The audit really is blind to it: audit.mjs:256 reads `cs.fontFamily.split(",")[0]`, i.e. the authored family, never the painted one. I also swept every rendered codepoint >= U+2000 across all seven states and the seat's scope claim holds exactly - U+2019, U+2014 and U+00B7 are all in Geist's cmap, so these four marks are the only text on the surface outside the two locked faces. And it is visible, not theoretical: a 4x capture of the rail shows the fallback pencil rendering as a SOLID FILLED shape against three outline marks, at a stroke weight and drawing convention matching nothing in ICON. SEVERITY is understated, not overstated: the seat filed refinement ("nothing is wrong"), but a filled glyph sitting in a four-item stack of outlines, drawn by a face outside the two the lock permits and changing per OS, is visibly wrong - this is a defect. One sub-claim does not reproduce here: I sampled the rail region at 4x for any pixel with saturation > 0.12 and found zero, so on this Windows build U+2611 resolves to a monochrome Segoe UI Symbol, not an emoji face. The seat hedged that as conditional, so it is not an error, but it is not evidence either. WHAT FAILS IS THE FIX. "Inline SVG paths at 13px ... on the same 12x12 grid as ICON" is self-contradictory and mis-sized. ICON's marks are authored `<svg width="12" height="12" viewBox="0 0 12 12">`, so they render at 12px and the "13px" is either ignored or, if forced, scales a 12-unit grid by 1.0833 and lands ICON's 1.5-1.6 strokes at 1.625 device px off the pixel grid at 1x - blurring hairlines on a surface whose entire icon system is deliberately integer-snapped. Worse, 12x12 is the wrong grid for this tile regardless of the scaling: .glyph chips are 20x20 carrying 12px marks (ratio 0.60), while .rail i is 26x26 (measured 26x26 at 1440). A 12px mark in a 26px tile is ratio 0.46 - the four rail marks would land visibly smaller and lighter than every other chip on the surface, and lighter than the fallback glyphs they replace, which optically fill ~14-15px today. The fix direction is right; its two numbers are both wrong.
sharpenedFix: Keep the direction - replace the four characters in shell()'s .rail markup with inline SVG in currentColor, aria-hidden, authored in ICON's stroke language - but fix the geometry. Draw on a 16x16 grid rendered at exactly 16px (`<svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 16 16">`), integer 1:1, which holds the 0.60 mark-to-tile ratio the 20px .glyph chips already establish (16/26 = 0.62). Hold stroke-width at 1.5 with stroke-linecap/linejoin round, identical to ICON.still/past/nobody/waiting, so the rail reads as the same pen rather than a scaled-up copy. Use `stroke="currentColor"` only - never ICON's hard-coded status hexes, which are reserved for the four status meanings and would import amber/red/indigo/emerald into inert furniture. currentColor is required, not optional, because .rail i.on inverts to color:var(--paper) on background:var(--ink). Then drop `font-size: 13px` from the .rail i rule: it no longer sets any type, and leaving a dead type declaration on a textless element is the kind of residue this lock exists to prevent. Redraw all four (including the arrow, which Geist does carry) so the set is one system, not three vectors beside one survivor.
breaks: Nothing in the behaviour gate: interaction-check.mjs contains no assertion touching .rail, and the nav is aria-hidden="true" so no accessible name, tab stop or focus order changes. The audit is where to re-measure. audit.mjs gates its family, weight, type-ramp and leading checks on `hasText && visible` (audit.mjs:253), so all four .rail i elements currently supply samples and would drop out entirely once the text is gone. Two consequences to re-run for: (1) the leading role-key map is keyed family|size|role (audit.mjs:287) - .rail i is presently a Geist|13|body occupant, and removing it changes which element is recorded as first-seen for that key, so re-run the audit and confirm no new leading collision surfaces elsewhere at 13px; (2) the AA contrast sample for ink-2 on --wash inside the rail chip disappears, because SVG strokes are not contrast-checked. That makes the gate easier, not harder, which is exactly the trap: verify by eye at 1x that 1.5px strokes in var(--ink-2) do not read lighter than the filled fallback glyphs they replace, and that the inverted .rail i.on mark in var(--paper) on var(--ink) still holds its weight. Also re-shoot light-full at 768x1024 and 1280x900 - the rail is display:none only below 560px, so it is in-frame at both - and re-run the dark variant, since currentColor inverts there and a stroke tuned on paper can go thin on ground. Palette is untouched: currentColor introduces no nineteenth hue.
